\mathbf{f}(x,z)=⟨x,\hspace{0.222em}6{x}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}\text{___}⟩

The vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(x,z)$ above parametrizes the parabolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $y=6{x}^{2}.$ What is the third component of $\mathbf{f}?$

Use the free parameter directly as its corresponding Cartesian coordinate.

For any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{f}(x,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨x,\hspace{0.222em}6{x}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}{\color{blue}z}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $x\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the third component of $\mathbf{f}$ is ${\color{blue}z}.$

Here the free parameter is $z$. The stated direct-coordinate convention therefore requires the third component to be $z$.
